The priest by the command of the law the right shoulder, etc., down to and Moses says in what follows.
8.29: 8.29 He took the breast. AUGUSTINE, question 23 on Leviticus. Above, because he commanded generally, etc., down to for from the beginning it is said: Be you to him in the things that pertain to the people, you to them in the things that pertain to God.
8.30: 8.30 And taking ointment. THE SAME, question 24. It is asked after the death of Moses who anointed the priest, etc., down to by obeying, not by excelling. He sprinkled, etc. Whatever goods are in us must be referred to him as to our head; hence: For them I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in truth. Openly therefore he called his passion sanctification, which sanctification is given to us. And upon the sons AUGUSTINE. It did not appear which of the sons succeeded the high priest. For Scripture does not define the firstborn or elder, unless in some divine judgment it was done, although it seems to have come from contention, that afterward there were several high priests, because when the more excellent contended, for the sake of ending the dispute the honor itself was granted to several.
8.31: 8.31 And the loaves also. He commanded the flesh to be eaten with the loaves, that we may understand the body of Christ, who is flesh, and the bread that came down from heaven, John 6., and this ought to be celebrated in the church only.
8.32: 8.32 Whatsoever remains. This we see done in the Church, and what remains unconsumed to be given to the fire. He does not say, however many days it remains unconsumed, that always, if it remain, it be given to the fire: hinting that if we fail in the eating of the sacrifice and cannot search whether what we see is the very body of the Lord, yet let us not leave it but give it to the fire, that the Holy Spirit may eat what we cannot. He eats however when we think possible to him what we cannot.
8.33: 8.33 From the door. It signifies that during the whole time of the present life one must not depart from the tabernacle, but persist in the service of God. AUGUSTINE, question 24 on Leviticus. At the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, etc., down to for habitation took this name. For seven, etc. ISICHIUS. The fiftieth, seven multiplied in itself, etc., down to observing the watches of the Lord, etc.
8.36: 8.36 And they did, etc. Aaron is joined to his sons, nor does he go out of the door of the tabernacle. For he was to be preached and in them to preach, as he himself consecrates and is consecrated in the members.
9.1: 9.1 On the eighth day, etc. The eighth day after the dedication signifies the day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit came, Acts 2. The seven days from the dedication hint seven times seven days, which were from the resurrection to Pentecost, namely 49, the day of Pentecost itself being added as an eighth. Pentecost, which fell on the day of the resurrection, bears the figure of the future, and of the consummation of the present age, because it revolves in seven days. For it was fitting that the Spirit come on the same day on which Christ rose. Then he says Aaron and his sons were called, and the elders: for then was convoked the spectacle of the Church, in which is Aaron, that is Christ, and his sons who are of high conduct, and therefore ministers of the priesthood, and the elders, that is the presbyters: of these the body of the Church consists.
9.2: 9.2 Take of, etc. Aaron takes a calf for a holocaust and a ram, and offers to the Lord. Then Christ made known his sacrifice when the Spirit coming gathered Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and the first-fruits of all nations into the upper room of the apostles, Acts 2. Aaron offers a calf and a ram when the doctors of the Church announce the mysteries of the passion and insinuate that they were celebrated for the salvation of the human race. Take. The apostles offered the he-goat on the day of Pentecost when Peter announcing penance said: Be converted and do penance. AUGUSTINE, question 26 on Leviticus. Take one he-goat of the goats, etc., down to but where all together, there also each, but is not converted.
9.6: 9.6 This is the word, etc. The word, namely, the thing commanded. Do this in commemoration of me, Luke 22. He says word, because more in the word is considered or consisted the dispensation of this mystery, and chiefly in the Lord's word transferring what appears into something greater and intelligible. Hence of the manna also he says: This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat, this is the word which the Lord has commanded, Exodus 16. In these therefore he signifies that the holy mystery, they acting and celebrating the Lord's supper, the Holy Spirit came. For it was the Lord's day on which it was fitting for the apostles to celebrate the sacred mysteries: whose traditions we following assign the Lord's day to divine assemblies. Likewise we find Christ manifest after the resurrection through the mystic supper and the breaking of bread.
9.7: 9.7 And offer for sin, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 27 on Leviticus. Another reading, etc., down to it is not necessary to be laid upon the holocaust. Offer the holocaust, etc. He does not say holocaust of consummation, as above, when it was offered that by sanctification he might be consummated, to perform the priesthood, which he was performing. It is to be noted that when sacrifices are offered for the people, sacrifices for sin are commanded to be offered, and holocaust and sacrifice of salvation. For the priest it was offered for sin and the holocaust of consummation, not of salvation. But the consummation was offered when the priests were sanctified. And these Moses offered for Aaron and his sons, but afterward Aaron already performing the priesthood is commanded to offer for himself a calf for sin, and a ram for a holocaust not of consummation; for then it was offered that by sanctification he might be consummated, and be able to perform the priesthood, which when he was performing, it was not necessary to consummate again.
9.8: 9.8 And immediately, etc. ISICHIUS. For what cause these sacrifices are also performed here we said above, etc., down to hence in the person of the priest we see both offered. AUGUSTINE, as above. It also moves that when Aaron made the gifts of the people which are mentioned above, etc., down to each from each living creature, as if he said breasts.
9.15: 9.15 And for sin, etc. ISICHIUS. Whose figure these have, etc., down to and they ceased not to meditate what would teach the Church. Stretching forth his hand, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 28 on Leviticus. Standing at the altar he served, etc., down to who forbade steps to be there.
9.22: 9.22 And thus finished and the rest. ISICHIUS. He evidently wishes to expound the whole figure of the Church, etc., down to the following show.
9.23: 9.23 And Moses and Aaron going into the tabernacle of the testimony, etc. THE SAME. Because of the intelligible tabernacle, etc., down to he is fit to give the blessing. And going in. He premised going in, and adds coming out, because the priest enters the tabernacle when he prays for himself or for the people, or is at leisure for divine contemplation; he comes out when he teaches, or blesses the people, or when he returns to conscience searching himself lest perhaps he offend in preaching. And the glory of the Lord appeared. In the appearance of fire, as on the day of Pentecost, hence he adds: And fire came forth from the Lord. Hence Luke too: There appeared to them parted tongues as of fire. To all the multitude, etc. To which Luke says the like: And when this voice was made, the multitude came together, and was confounded in mind, Acts 2.; not only came together but was afraid. Hence here it follows: And they were astonished and wondered, etc. Which were upon the altar. He found that it is necessary to lay the aforesaid sacrifices and their expositions upon the intelligible altar of the body of Christ, that our intention may sigh thither, and then the nourishments of the intelligible fire, that is of the Holy Spirit, will be present, of whom it is said: Our God is a consuming fire, Deuteronomy 4.
10.1: 10.1 And Nadab. AUGUSTINE, question 31 on Leviticus, vol. 3. The fire coming out from the Lord the sons of Aaron died, etc., down to they shall suffer torments. And taking, etc. ISIDORE, questions on Leviticus, vol. 5. They offer strange fire, etc., down to lest we burn with vices. ISICHIUS. Here those who teach strange things, etc., down to whence they could merit life. AUGUSTINE, as above. Another reading, etc., down to through whom he gave us Scripture.
10.4: 10.4 And calling Mishael and Elzaphan. Mishael, touching of God. Elzaphan, or Elzaphan, illumination of God, or mirror of God. To these it is rightly commanded to carry Nadab and Abihu out of the camp. For these signify the saints, who, illumined by God, touch him with the hands of faith, and contemplate God with perfect faith. Hence well are they called sons of Uzziel, which signifies the Gospel: hence he is said to have been Aaron's cousin, because great is the kinship of the Gospel and the Law. For the Gospel is the exposition of the Law: and the sons of the Gospel thrust out the truly dead heretics from the camp of the Church. Or Misadai and Elzaphan the first the touching of God, that is Misadai; Elzaphan is interpreted watchtower of my God. Whoever knows how to touch God, and to behold Christ, the flesh namely and divinity, like Thomas who, touching the flesh with the hand, said: My Lord and my God, John 20., can take away the fire of strange doctrine from the face of the saints, that is of the priests. The tunics of the priests, the conduct and life by which they are clothed with the habit of the priesthood. They are cast away therefore with the priesthood from the fellowship of the priests and also of the people. Hence he adds, outside the tabernacle, that is the church of the people, the sons of the paternal uncle of Aaron do this. Aaron, that is David, by whom the prophecies are understood, which make Christ manifest, and in a way bring forth to the ignorant. The brother of prophecy is the Gospel; for what was done in the Gospels was foretold by the prophets. The sons therefore of the brother of the father Aaron, that is of the Gospel, eject such. Hence: If any come to you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into the house, 2 John.
10.6: 10.6 The heads, etc. According to the letter. Because they had lately been consecrated to God, he commands that they not lay aside the holy vestments, but stand by ready to serve God. Allegorically, however, that they make no division of persons in Christ. For the head of Christ is God, but Christ consists of divinity and humanity; the tiara of the head, that is of the divinity, is the humanity, with which the divinity was covered as with a cap; this is not to be taken away, nor division of persons in Christ preached, but one person of two substances. Your heads, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 32 on Leviticus. Lest, namely, they lay aside the cidaris, etc., down to hence he adds: Your brethren and all the house of Israel shall bewail the burning. ISICHIUS. We are not ignorant what the cidaris signify, etc., down to of which: His anointing teaches you of all things.
10.9: 10.9 Wine and anything that may inebriate. THE SAME. Up to now the Church keeps this law, etc., down to that is spiritually inspired. Wine and anything, etc. They are commanded to abstain from what casts down or overthrows the state of mind, when they enter the tabernacle. But let us never be drunk, but always sober in mind and body. When you shall enter. AUGUSTINE, question 33. When then was it lawful for them to drink, etc., down to that this be the lawful office of the priests forever in their generations.
10.10: 10.10 That you may have knowledge to discern. AUGUSTINE. This also is placed ambiguously, etc., down to or rather is it to be referred to both?
10.12: 10.12 Take the sacrifice, etc. ISICHIUS. That the breast confidence, etc., down to but what pertains to the peace and salutary offerings belongs to the whole people. Take, etc. The secrets, namely, and deep mysteries of Scripture which the crowd cannot grasp are to be retained and eaten by the perfect; beside the altar, that is beside the faith and authority of the Lord's passion.
10.14: 10.14 The breast, etc. AUGUSTINE, question 34. The breast. Although names have been given to each, etc., down to from the breast was laid on the altar.
10.16: 10.16 Meanwhile. ISICHIUS. Because every sin is blotted out by penance, and those who committed the aforesaid sin of another doctrine and blasphemy were not saved, the lawgiver expounds the cause of their death. Meanwhile the he-goat, namely because the sons of Aaron did not eat what was for sin in the holy place, that is, they did not make the penance of the sin committed to be performed in the church. To whom this command is given, whom Christ has appointed in the Church as his vicars. For he himself offered the blood of his oblation, which was offered for our blood, into the holy, that is into heaven, in the sight of the Father. This sacrifice ought to be eaten in the holy place, that is the church, for the propitiation of sins, hence he adds: As it was commanded me, that is as I commanded. For Moses bears the person of Christ. He found it burnt, because they had sinned against the Holy Spirit, the offering for penance was taken away by the intelligible fire of the Holy Spirit. For to those sinning willfully there remains no sacrifice for sin, Hebrews 10. For as true penance merits pardon, so feigned penance provokes God: for the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, Wisdom 1. The holy Fathers called this the irremissible sin and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, to persevere in crimes to the end of life, to despair of one's salvation, to distrust the power and mercy of the Redeemer. ADAMANTIUS. Not to sin belongs to God alone, etc., down to unless true and sincere. AUGUSTINE, question 36 on Leviticus. Since six animals are commanded to be offered for the people, etc., down to all which had been for sin.
10.19: 10.19 Aaron answered, etc. In the person of the Church, whose figure he bears, as also of Christ, Aaron seems to say this. As if, because after the coming of the Savior they were deputed to minister, and to offer for penance, and to expound the prophetic life. Otherwise: The teachers perished and in them these things befell the Church, that she bewail the death of priests and masters, hence she could not today eat for sin, nor pray: but it displeased the Lord. AUGUSTINE. Aaron answered, etc. If today they offered what is for their sin, etc., down to But why this was done, Aaron answered, and it pleased Moses. Today. As if to say: if before the remission of the Savior they had so sinned, perhaps it would be pardoned, when knowledge was not yet manifested to the world: hence, If I had not come, and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin, John 15.
11.1: 11.1 The Lord spoke. ISICHIUS. Whatever is made by God is clean by the very authority of the institution. In animals therefore the morals of men are painted, and acts, and wills, from which they become clean or unclean. THE SAME. The Lord said to Noah: Everything that moves and lives shall be meat for you, Genesis 9., etc. In Genesis also it is said: God saw all things that he had made, and they were very good, Genesis 1. Here, however, some are forbidden as evil, and decreed unclean. Yet these are not contrary to each other: for the Lord briefly restrains the gluttony of the Jews, and the spiritual exposition of the precepts instructs what they ought to be. For the law is nourishment of the rational soul rationally understood. As above through the offerings he figured the offerers, so now through what is eaten he expresses the eaters.
11.3: 11.3 Everything that has, etc. ISIDORE. In fishes whatever has not fins and scales is abominable: rough things are counted for clean. For bristly and hairy, firm and grave morals of men are approved. Those without them are called unclean, to whom light and slippery, weak and effeminate morals are added. He also joins fins and scales; for whatever fishes are finned and scaly. If to some ignorance is soluble, to these also sublime knowledge and heavenly life: but those who are not such, with these not even to take food. Morally. GREGORY. Fishes that have fins and scales are wont to leap over the waters. In finned fishes therefore the elect souls are figured, which alone pass into the body of the heavenly Church; which, supported by the fins of virtues, leap through heavenly desire to contemplation, although they fall back into themselves through the fragility of the flesh. They alone pass into the body of the elect as choice food, who, while they serve the lowest things, climb to heavenly things by leaps of mind, lest they always lie hid in the depths of cares, where they have no care of the highest love, as of free air. Those therefore who are occupied with temporal things then dispose outward things well when they anxiously take refuge in the inward, nor love the noise of disturbance, but rest in themselves within in the bosom of tranquility.
11.10: 11.10 Whatsoever fins, etc. There are also fishes having a shell in place of skin, whose scale cannot be taken off, because neither by the word of God do they lay aside the scales of ignorance, nor receive the knife of the spirit: and though they are found in the sea of baptism, or in the rivers of penance, yet they are abominable in those things which move and live in the waters, because the regeneration and life which they received in baptism they corrupt by living ill.
11.11: 11.11 Flesh. RABANUS on Leviticus. When he forbids the swine, etc., down to seeking the darkness of night.
11.13: 11.13 These are of the fowls, etc. ISICHIUS. What pertains to the life of the contemplative he adds, etc., down to little women laden with sins.
11.14: 11.14 The vulture according to its kind. THE SAME. Who delights in wars. Hence follows the army, expecting the corpses of the dead: he ought not to feed on another's mourning who gives himself to contemplation.
11.16: 11.16 The ostrich. The ostrich is a bird, but cannot fly, and is always about the earth, like some who serve God and entangle themselves in secular business, Job 39; 2 Timothy 2. The owl. They say this sees sharply by night and little by day. Such are those who glory in the contemplation of the Law, and cannot take in the light of the Gospel. The night raven. It plunders only by night. Such are the nations gaping after the works of the night, which are fornication, uncleanness, impudicity, Galatians 5. The gull. The gull is an animal dwelling in water as on land: for it flies and swims. To this are likened those who venerate circumcision and baptism. The hawk. The hawk is among the birds of prey, but grows tame, and does its plunder with men. This is imitated by those who seem meek but strive to plunder with the powerful and covetous and rapacious. The cormorant and the ibis. These have long necks, and as is said draw food from the depth of earth or water, nor are they to be imitated. For he who is at leisure for contemplation ought to tend to higher things, nor be anxious about lower.
11.19: 11.19 The hoopoe. This is mournful and loving mourning. The sorrow of the world works death. But he who loves God ought to rejoice, pray without ceasing, in all things give thanks, 1 Thessalonians 5. The bat. Which flies about the earth, uses wings for feet: which is foreign to those who contemplate, lest their contemplation be occupied with earthly things.
11.20: 11.20 Every thing of fowls that goes upon four feet, etc. Those who seem like the contemplative, but like creeping things cling to earthly concupiscences, even if they walk on four feet, that is if they pretend the evangelical preaching which calls to penance; because they do not truly embrace the social life, serving pleasures, are abominable.
11.21: 11.21 But whatever goes, etc. Because though they are in the flesh, they do not walk according to the flesh, 2 Corinthians 10., but leap from filthy actions, and are mingled with earthly men, to instruct and teach: as the Lord with sinners and publicans, Matthew 9. We ought to have legs higher than feet, lest we halt on both feet, as the Jews in the law and the prophets; but let us have straight legs, like the Cherubim, of whom it is said: Their legs were straight, and their feet winged, Ezekiel 1.
11.22: 11.22 The bruchus. Which leaps, but less than the attacus or locust, which leap more. Such are those who converse with sinners, for conversion, not for consent or imitation. The ophiomachus. Who fights with serpents, but our fight is with the ancient serpent and his angels, Apocalypse 12.
11.25: 11.25 That he may carry. As he who calls evil good, and bitter sweet, Isaiah 5.: for by praising the evil which he ought to have forbidden, he makes it his own and carries it.
11.26: 11.26 Every beast which. ISICHIUS. The law passes over no sin; whatever are forbidden in the Gospel are expressed in the enigmas of the Law, that in the mouth of two witnesses every word may stand, Matthew 18., and in both laws you may praise God, and, as he forbids, flee evil.
11.27: 11.27 That which goes upon hands, etc. He who migrates the evangelical conversation, but walks on hands, for the sake of base gain, namely, laying on hands, 1 Timothy 4., he is rightly compared to all beasts, so that you may call him adulterer, or covetous, murderer and the like: for he communicates in all by the wicked laying on of hands.
11.28: 11.28 He that shall carry such carcasses. By giving false testimony, calling the unworthy worthy, and the clean unclean.
11.29: 11.29 The weasel. Gluttony. For the mouse avoids no dangers for the gluttony of its belly. The crocodile. Which, of hard skin and malicious, feeds on mud.
11.30: 11.30 The chameleon. It shows pity, and for weakness feigns itself gentle, when it is cruel. The mole. A blind animal born of the earth. For it is created, they say, of rained-on and muddy earth, but first corrupt.
11.31: 11.31 He that shall touch, etc. If they were naturally unclean, he would be unclean who touched even the living. The carcasses of such are actions, that is guile, theft, duplicity, and the like, in which is death of the soul.
11.32: 11.32 And upon what, etc. ISICHIUS. The lawgiver uses an admirable division, etc., down to both wooden vessel and garment.
11.34: 11.34 All meat, etc. By meat and drink he understands good works, therefore he said: The meat that you shall eat, and the liquid that is drunk, etc. Because both food and drink of evil actions are forbidden, that no one partake. If therefore on good actions, which are in every vessel, that is in every man, any carcass fall, necessarily the action will be unclean. For if on a good action pride, guile, hypocrisy or any carcass, that is bringing death to the one partaking, fall, this too will be unclean: for an evil intention falling on a good action pollutes it. If water be poured upon it. AUGUSTINE, question 37 on Leviticus. Of the vessel, namely, which was made unclean from unclean carcasses if perhaps it had water. Water. Of baptism: for the discourse is of the baptized; of unbelievers he makes no mention. Hence Paul: I wrote to you not to mingle with fornicators, 1 Corinthians 3., not certainly the fornicators of this world, etc.
11.35: 11.35 Or ovens. By this are designated teachers, in whom the foods of sacred doctrine are cooked by the operation and fire of the Holy Spirit. Nor is it wonderful: Moab is called a cauldron: Moab the pot of my hope, Romans 2. Chytropodes, etc. Because those who teach not to steal, steal; and those who preach not to commit adultery, commit adultery: yet the doctrine is clean. Hence fountains and the rest.
11.37: 11.37 If it fall. ISICHIUS. He leaves nothing unexamined, etc., down to if any carcass fall upon them, they become unclean.
11.39: 11.39 He that shall touch the carcass thereof shall be unclean. ISICHIUS. We ought to abominate the life of the wicked, to imitate that of the just. For he who touches the life of the wicked shall be unclean until he repents.
11.40: 11.40 He that shall eat. That is, as an advocate defended, and in helping transferred to himself, let him wash his garments, that is wicked actions, until he repent.
11.41: 11.41 Every thing that creeps upon the earth. This the lawgiver expounded above, but to the frequent meditation of the law, admonishing the hearer, he repeats.
11.47: 11.47 And that you may know what to eat. These foods do not cleanse or pollute us, but we ourselves: for we give life to what is eaten, and as every food is good, 1 Peter 2., and nothing is to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving; so what is eaten, that is what nourishes the soul, good actions namely, we give life to, if we use them well: if ill, we put them to death. For he who makes alms from robbery puts it to death, and takes away its power; and those who abstain from foods, but detract from their brethren, put abstinence to death.
12.2: 12.2 If a woman, having received seed. ISIDORE, questions on Leviticus, vol. 5. The week is the present life, etc., down to nor in the future will be purified. She shall be unclean. ISICHIUS. Because, namely, the sower is unclean, as heir of Adam, who by transgression was unclean, and thus mixed with his wife. For after he went out of paradise he knew his wife, and so the human race is propagated. Seven days. THE SAME. Because Adam, etc., down to when Adam, separated from paradise, fell into this misery. On the eighth day, etc. THE SAME. The eighth day, etc., down to But disobedience contracted uncleanness and filth for us.
12.4: 12.4 Thirty-three days, etc. THE SAME. Seven being added, etc., down to for it is uncertain whether they bear a female or a male. AUGUSTINE, question 40 on Leviticus. What difference is there between seven days, etc., down to in a female eighty. She shall touch nothing holy. What does he mean to understand by sanctuary, since none but priests ought to enter the tabernacle, and up to the second veil: beyond the veil, however, where the ark was, the high priest alone entered? Perhaps before the tabernacle, where the altar of sacrifices is, it could be called a sanctuary. For often the court also is called a holy place, when it is said: In the holy place they shall eat them. Thither perhaps women entered offering their gifts, to lay on the altar.
12.6: 12.6 And when the days are fulfilled. He opens the intention, because, namely, natural motions do not make pollution, but sin, of which David says: Behold I was conceived in iniquities, Psalm 50., etc., calling nature mother, and signifying that the uncleanness of the sin of Adam and Eve descended on the whole human race. Therefore Moses, the days of purification fulfilled, commanded a holocaust and a sacrifice for sin to be immolated; plainly showing that the image of God gives perfection to our race. For the days of cleansing show the formation, the holocaust the perfection. AUGUSTINE, as above. Is it a sin to have borne? etc., down to not that they might say for a son or daughter, but for a son or daughter. It is to be noted how poor the Lord willed to be born, that for him there should be offered not a lamb and a young pigeon or turtledove, but a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons according to the Gospel, which the Scripture of Leviticus then commanded to be offered if the hand of the offerer had not a lamb, which is great enough. BEDE, on Leviticus, vol. 2. Our Lord not only man, etc., down to and afterward to the heavenly Jerusalem, commended to the Lord by the victims of good works, she shall come.
